summary: _(ii) Pass any orders this Hon’ble Commission may deem just and equitable in favour of the Petitioner.”_ _19. Accordingly, we are of the opinion that Respondent BEST has not fully adhered to our directives outlined in the Final Orders. Therefore, we direct JITPL to raise a revised invoice, aligning with the Final Orders, for the outstanding payment owed by BEST after_ _28. In the present case also, the order under execution dated 5.11.2018 read with the corrigendum dated 3.12.2018, as already noted above, does not contain the grant of any LPS to the Petitioner herein, hence, it would not be appropriate to issue any direction awarding such relief at the stage of the present proceedings._ 15. On a specific query by the Commission as to whether the question of arbitrability of the dispute (whether tariff or non-tariff) has been addressed by the parties, the learned counsel for JIPL, while answering in the negative, sought time to file its submissions on the same. The learned counsel for BEST, while pointing out that the matter pertains to LPS, submitted that it has also raised the issue of limitation with regard to the claim of JIPL and sought time to file its written submissions, including the question of the arbitrability of the disputes. The Commission adjourned the hearing of the Petition after directing JIPL and BEST to file their written submissions, including the question of ‘arbitrability’ of the disputes. 19. The Commission, after a virtual hearing of the submissions of the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondent BEST, that the matter is required to be adjudicated by the Commission, reserved its order on ‘maintainability’. 21. We have examined the submissions of the parties. Section 79(1)(f) of the Act provides as under: _(1) A judicial authority, before which an action is brought in a matter which is the subject of an arbitration agreement shall, if a party to the arbitration agreement or any person claiming through or under him, so applies not later than the date of submitting his first statement on the substance of the dispute, then, notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of the Supreme Court or any Court, refer the parties to arbitration unless it finds that prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists._ 24. It is noticed that the Commission vide its order dated 5.11.2018 in Petition No.159 / MP/2017, has upheld the jurisdiction of the Commission to adjudicate the disputes with regard to the change in law compensation, in terms of section 79(1)(b) read with section 79(1)(f) of the Act. No PPA/PSA has been executed by the parties in the present case. to be adjudicated through arbitration, then it is for the Commission to nominate the arbitrator(s) on an application filed by either party. As stated above, there is no valid arbitration agreement between the parties, and the parties have also not filed any application seeking reference of the disputes to arbitration. There is also no consensual acceptance of the parties to the dispute to refer the said matter to arbitration. In fact, the Commission in its order dated 5.11.2018 has held that the disputes relating to the change in law compensation in terms of the LOI dated 14.1.2016 is to be adjudicated by the Commission in terms of Section 79(1)(b) read with section 79(1)(f) of the Act. In the present case, JIPL/TPTCL has sought the payment of LPS, on account of the delay on the part of BEST to make the differential payments of the CIL claims (increase in CEC), in terms of the CIL order 5.11.2018/ 3.12.2018 and the interim order of APTEL dated 26. BEST in the present petition has also raised issues on merit, stating that the claims of JITPL are barred by limitation and are also hit by the principles of constructive res judicata. Having held that the petition is maintainable, as above, we ‘admit’ the petition and direct the listing of the petition to hear the parties on merits, during the second week of July 2025, for which a separate notice will be issued to the parties. Pleadings shall be completed by the parties, if not done earlier.
title: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 7 of the Letter of Intent dated 14.1.2016 issued by Brihan Mumbai Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking (BEST) to Tata Power Trading Company Ltd seeking directions of payment of late payment surcharge on account of delay by BEST in honoring the invoice(s) raised by Petitioner towards claiming additional expenditure incurred by it on account of increase in Clean Energy Cess (CEC) and interest thereupon. Jindal India Power Limited
